refusals: THE RECORDING PREDATES THIS ORDERING. Every median in measurements/update-floor.published.json was taken under the OLD order — a rigid rotation, `phases[(k + shift) % length]`, which never changed the cyclic order and so gave every phase one fixed predecessor for a whole run. That is what made an ADJACENT null read 0.0001 µs and a FAR null with the same true value of ZERO read 9.3750 µs. Numbers from that file and numbers from this run MAY NOT BE QUOTED SIDE BY SIDE — not in a table, not in a ratio, not in a sentence. Quoting across a changed instrument is the error this repository has already made twice. Re-record before comparing, and rewrite the banner below from the new file in the same change.

(Q4), the cross-check this file most wanted tested, printed a verdict on a difference the SAME run refused as under its own resolution bar — the renderer-scale null was 9.3750 µs, 7.8% of its own row. THIRD PREDICTION (R1-R6) — NEVER RUN. The recording carries reorder with four rows. No reading of R1-R6 exists anywhere; what to distrust in their first run is written above their falsifiers in this file, under WHAT TO DISTRUST IN THE FIRST RUN.

FOURTH PREDICTION (Q7-Q11) — NEVER RUN either, and it is the one that judges the INSTRUMENT rather than a number: the recording carries wide with NINE rows and this file declares ELEVEN. On that recording TWO of wide's five attributions were refused by a bar that a null with a true value of ZERO put at 37.5 µs, and RAISING THE BATCH CANNOT MOVE A BIAS — every number here is µs PER TRANSITION, so multiplying reps divides the region by the same factor it multiplies it. (Q7) is what asks whether that null is measuring the instrument or measuring where a row was declared.

AND THE UNIT: MICROSECONDS PER TRANSITION. mount-floor, ssr-floor and hydrate-floor all report MILLISECONDS PER REP. Published pages have already taken the wrong one from this file and been out by 1000× with both documentation gates green, because neither gate checks a unit; how far that ran is recorded in docs-site/docs/decisions/upd-07-the-general-path-and-its-subsequence.md.
